reasons.9: All parts are there: PRD, stack table with Why and Switch-when columns, tokens.ts, S1 to S8 specs and T1 to T10. One cross-reference is wrong: the architecture Risks say 'T6 tests two parallel calls', but the concurrency test is in T3.

A.top_fix: Fix the ticket reference in 02-technical-architecture.md Risks (the overbooking test is T3, not T6). Also add a phone screenshot of the #taken or #error state so the recovery path is visible in the screens and not only in the spec.

reasons.3: Most of the first phone view is empty address boxes and a three-line intro. The booking choice itself (date hint, Arrival time options) is cut off under the bottom bar, so the 'key screen' shows little of what makes this a booking.
reasons.6: The spec defines error, storage-failure and sending states, but the prototype only shows the empty form. The reply itself marks Recovery and Navigation as Fail because a sent request has no change or cancel route (D-12).
reasons.7: The 390px view works and the checker is clean. But the mockup uses a desktop-style native mm/dd/yyyy date input, and in desktop.png the 844px phone frame pushes Continue below the fold. The form also scrolls inside a fixed frame, so phone-full.png never shows the Arrival time group.
reasons.9: PRD, security, screen specs and tickets are there. The stack table gives sources (D-04, 'Proposed') instead of reasons. Tokens exist only as prose in DESIGN.md, with no code token file for Cursor to import.
reasons.10: T1 to T4 have a bounded change and acceptance checks. T5 and T7 to T10 are only one 'Acceptance checks' line, with no goal, files, build steps or stop point. They rely on a separate prompt template in build-rules.md, so they cannot be pasted into Cursor as they stand.

B.top_fix: Rewrite T5 to T12 as full paste-ready prompts (goal, files to read, build steps, do-not-add list, acceptance checks, stop). Also make the prototype show the When group and arrival choice above the fold, not just empty address fields.

why: A shows a real booking decision screen (day chips, full/selected time windows, summary, one primary) and pairs it with paste-ready tickets that each have a goal, files, rules, checks and a stop point. B's key screen is mostly empty address fields, and most of its tickets are only lists of acceptance checks.
